test.name: userPresent: no resolves a weak match downward, on a wrap-up
test.description: Plan section B2. The downward resolution used to key on 'an autonomous run where no user can ever confirm'. A wrap-up has the researcher present and still needs it, so the rule now keys on the delegation's `userPresent: no`. `ut_person_evidence_023` is the autonomous half of this; this is the wrap-up half, and it is the case the old wording could not express.

input.delegation:
The researcher is wrapping this question up. Link assertion a_002 (the Patrick Flynn baptism record) to the right person in the tree, or handle it per the threshold policy if it should not be linked.

userPresent: no
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: `userPresent: no` is what makes the downward resolution apply. The researcher being mid-conversation is irrelevant: they asked to wrap up, so there is nobody to pause with on THIS link.
A weak match, or one capped at `speculative` by a qualitative conflict, becomes a NO-LINK: no `pe_` entry, and no rejection recorded either — only the researcher records one.
The absence of a user never upgrades confidence. Linking at `probable` to close the question off is the failure this rule exists for.
The returned summary names the candidate, the score, and what conflicted, so the researcher can pick it up later.
